plan.title: AD lesional vs control: hallmark pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The DESeq2 results table (de_results.csv, 12000 genes, treated=AD lesional vs control contrast) already holds the differential expression test, so this plan starts from it rather than re-fitting a model, per the research question's instruction. Step 1 runs a sample-structure QC (blind VST + PCA + sample distance heatmap) on the raw Salmon gene counts to characterize the design and flag sample_01 (library size ~4x below median) before any downstream interpretation leans on it — this is descriptive context for the enrichment result, not a re-test. Step 2 ranks all 12000 tested genes by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat column) from de_results.csv and runs preranked GSEA (gseapy) against the MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets (50 sets, 2026.1 release, staged locally), with the standard 15-500 gene size window and BH-adjusted FDR. Step 3 produces the enrichment report: significant hallmark pathways, direction (treated vs control, with the contrast's reference level and sign convention stated explicitly), leading-edge genes per significant set, the method-dependence caveat, and a full reproducibility record (package versions, seed, collection version).

flags.message: If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
